newsitem.title: USA: IDT fined over billing, ads - N.Y. state.
newsitem.headline: IDT fined over billing, ads - N.Y. state.

text.p: IDT Corp., a national Internet access provider, will pay five states a total of $250,000 in penalties and give customers refunds as part of a settlement regarding its billing and advertising practices, New York state Attorney General Dennis Vacco said Wednesday.
IDT, meanwhile, announced it had fired 140 employees, more than a fourth of its work force, as part of its shift away from Internet access and back toward its telecommunications roots.

Under the settlement, Hackensack, N.J.-based IDT will provide refunds to customers for unexpected long-distance charges for Internet access and technical support and for customers who dropped the service but received bills anyway, Vacco said in a statement.
IDT has about 150,000 customers nationwide. It is known for ads promising "uncensored" Internet access to adult and other material on the Internet.
The settlement also forbids IDT from running advertisements that misrepresent its rates and services, the attorney general said.

"The growing demand for online service has created a difficult situation for many providers who are having trouble keeping up," Vacco said. "But consumers have the right to services they are being promised and are paying for."
The $250,000 will be split equally by New York, New Jersey, Iowa, Tennessee and Texas, a spokesman for Vacco said. Michigan, which joined the group late, will not share in the penalties.
The settlement comes about a year after the states first looked into the matter.
"I am very happy that this issue was resolved amicably with the attorneys general," IDT President Jim Courter said in a statement.
The settlement recalled an agreement reached Jan. 29 between No. 1 online service America Online Inc. and the attorneys general of 36 states, including Vacco.
America Online offered refunds and credits to customers frustrated by busy signals when they tried to log on. America Online has about 8 million members.

IDT said it fired 120 employees, mostly in sales and marketing for dial-up Internet access, and 20 administrative employees as part of its shift away from Internet access and toward telecommunications, which it said had steadily become increasingly profitable.
"We regret having to take these measures, but it is essential in order to maintain a competitive business in an ever-changing industry," IDT Chairman and founder Howard Jonas said in the statement.

In telecommunications, IDT is perhaps best known for its pioneering international call-back services, which cut the cost of overseas calling. The call-back business takes advantage of overseas long-distance reseller pacts to exploit national phone rate differences, allowing calls to be made at U.S.-level tariffs.

IDT also offers Net2Phone, which allows people with multimedia computers to make calls to regular telephones over the Net at much lower costs than traditional long-distance calls. IDT stock dipped 12.5 cents to $7.875 on Nasdaq.
